annotation.summary_en: A young lecturer attempts to discourage village residents from drinking using a biological example, only for a local to offer a literal-minded rebuttal.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: In a community hall during the day, a young presenter dressed in a shirt and tie stands before a seated audience of older men. He is delivering an animated presentation against alcoholism, supported by a whiteboard displaying percentage charts and statistics. He explains that while general alcohol usage is at 30%, it rises to 70% in villages, prompting the Council of Europe to intervene. To conclude his lecture, he proposes a 'natural' example involving livestock to prove that alcohol is harmful. He asks the audience of cattle breeders: if you place one bucket of water and one bucket of vodka in front of an animal, which one will it drink? A man in the audience, wearing a plaid shirt, responds correctly that the animal would drink the water. When the lecturer triumphantly asks 'Why?', expecting a response about health or instinct, the villager bluntly retorts, 'Because he's an animal, an animal!' implying only a beast would choose water over vodka. The sketch ends with this subversion of the lecturer's logic.
